title: Windowed commit-log producer for streaming + bulk embedding ingestion
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a windowed commit-log producer and complementary consumer pipeline to support streaming and bulk embedding ingestion with strong idempotency guarantees, bounded memory backpressure, and fast tail latency. This work enables a single API surface for small streaming producers and large bulk uploads while preserving exactly-once semantic goals for downstream vector stores and reranking jobs.
background: Current embedding ingest endpoints handle either small streaming rows or large batch imports but we lack a unified producer model that: 1) supports client-side streaming with mid-stream checkpoints, 2) enables efficient server-side batching for GPUs, and 3) provides deterministic deduplication on retries. Production customers have reported duplicate vectors after retry storms and increased p99 ingestion latency during bursts. A commit-log approach with windowed commits and checkpointable offsets should address these issues and simplify async job orchestration.
acceptance_criteria: 1) API: New /v2/embeddings/append endpoint accepts windowed chunks with an idempotency_key per chunk and optional customer_id header. 2) Reliability: Retry a failed chunk up to 5x without producing duplicate vectors; observed duplicate rate < 0.1% in canary. 3) Latency: Median server-side commit latency for streaming append < 40ms and p99 < 450ms under 10k rps producer load. 4) Scaling: Consumer worker can batch and commit > 20k vectors/s per pod with autoscaling rules. 5) Observability: Dashboards for ingestion_latency_p50/p90/p99, chunk_retry_count, duplicate_rate, and consumer_backpressure. 6) Migration: Dual-write canary (5% of traffic) validated and rollback procedure documented.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: API + producer SDK changes (2 weeks) - design chunk envelope, schema version, idempotency_key semantics, and server-side append handler. Add producer SDK helpers for chunking large payloads and emitting commit markers. Phase 2: Commit-log storage and checkpointing (1 week) - implement append-only windowed commit log in durable store (S3-backed segments + metadata in Dynamo/Spanner) with atomic window checkpoints. Phase 3: Consumer worker & dedupe store (2 weeks) - build consumer that reads committed windows, reconstructs vectors, writes to vector-store with per-embedding dedupe check via idempotency index with TTL and sharding. Phase 4: Canary, perf testing, and roll-out (1 week) - run shadow traffic, 5% canary, load tests up to target throughput, and finalize metrics and dashboards. Phase 5: Docs + SDK release + console integration (1 week).
tasks: Design API contract: chunk schema, idempotency_key, seq_no, window_id, final_chunk flag
Produce SDK changes: Node/Python/Go helpers for streaming chunking and resumable retries
Implement server append handler with backpressure and per-client window limits
Durable windowed commit-log: segment writer + atomic window checkpointing
Consumer worker: window reader, batcher, dedupe-index writer, vector-store writer
Idempotency index: sharded, eventually-evicting store keyed by (customer_id, idempotency_key)
E2E tests: replay-resume tests, duplicate-insert fuzz tests, failure-in-the-middle scenarios
Load testing harness: synthetic producers with configurable burstiness and chunk sizes
Console/dashboard: ingestion metrics, per-customer lag, failed-chunk alerts
Migration plan: dual-write flag, canary rollout runbook, rollback steps
risks: 1) Durability/latency tradeoff for commit-log: S3-backed segments reduce cost but increase tail latency for commit fencing. 2) Idempotency index blowup for very large customer workloads if TTL/cleanup is misconfigured. 3) Backpressure interaction with client SDKs: poorly implemented client retries could cause head-of-line blocking. 4) Vector-store hot-sharding during consumer bursts may require temporary re-sharding or rate limiting.
mitigations: Use a two-tier commit: fast mem-segment + async durable flush to S3 for most windows; enforce per-customer window concurrency limits; implement idempotency index TTL and cardinality monitoring; add producer-side jittered retries and exponential backoff. Run staged load tests and tune batch sizes and consumer parallelism before canary expansion.
notes: We will adopt existing embedders' schema for vector payloads to avoid conversion costs. Chunk size best-practice target: 256–1,024 vectors per chunk for optimal GPU packing. Provide 'append' vs 'replace' mode flags for backfills where dedupe is not desired. Consider optional checksum in chunk envelope to detect silent corruption.
